result.report:
PASS for the stated partial scope: exact compact ordinary-form descent in every bidegree, componentwise purity after completed-algebraic scalar extension, and the ordinary zero-Hessian current equivalence in every pure dimension n≥1. This does not certify classical recognition or solve the original P06.2 problem.

I checked the supporting argument independently. The essential imported statements were checked against the authentic [CLD v2 full text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) and the [published Ducros article](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1142/S1793744212500077.pdf). The indexed premises below record analytic foundations, not predecessor verdicts or the conclusions being audited. The quotations reproduce supplied excerpts checked against those primary bodies. For boundary applications, the independently opened CLD 11.4.1 supplies all necessary statements; the repeated Berkovich citation adds no indispensable premise.

The finite algebra calculations work with the actual algebras. Bounded basis-coordinate maps establish the finite tensor topology and completeness, including nilpotents. The field-norm existence and uniqueness arguments are valid. The Galois invariant calculation uses kernels rather than averaging in the valued field. The separable prime calculation identifies every minimal component through field factors; the purely inseparable calculation gives an inclusion-preserving prime correspondence through b↦b^q. The integral dimension argument supplies the required equality of component dimensions. These calculations establish finite-stage purity, rather than merely total dimension.

The finite-Galois induction closes. The actual residue tensor has a transitive G-action on its field factors, and the stabilizer calculation gives the specified embedding E^H⊂H(x). The quotient-Banach Newton construction lifts that embedding to an actual analytic neighborhood: the denominator and derivative inverse bounds come from rational localization relations, and the stated contraction estimates remain valid with nilpotents. The equivalent F-homogeneous norm and Tate presentation establish the local F-analytic structure. Common rational neighborhoods identify the ordinary analytic germs and forms. Relative-interior composition gives boundarylessness over F, and same-carrier calibration restriction then gives precisely the cancellable real factor [F:K]. The tensor product decomposition produces the smaller Galois extensions required by induction.

At the fixed locus, transitivity really makes the scalar fibre a singleton, so full-fibre shrinking applies. Orbit norm units descend as actual units, with their inverses. The real averaging projection matches the coefficient restriction to the fixed linear subspace; it does not assert invariant-form descent. The compact partition produces norm-matched tests, coefficient forms restricting to zero on that subspace, and an off-fixed-locus remainder. All zero extensions have supports compactly contained in their defining ordinary opens.

The collar estimate covers all ranks and n=1. For rank zero the restricted form and its tangential derivatives vanish. For rank at least two, collar volume O(δ^r) absorbs second cutoff derivatives O(δ^-2). For rank one, exterior repetition removes every component containing a transverse generator from the second-cutoff term; the surviving tangential coefficient is O(δ) because its restriction at t=0 is zero. Thus that term has uniformly bounded L1 norm. The comparison point may lie outside the polytope, and the global coefficient extensions supplied in the argument address this explicitly.

The total-variation estimate follows by taking absolute values separately on positively calibrated skeletal sheets. It does not follow from cancellation in a signed pushforward. Compact chart refinements give finitely many relevant sheets and fixed constants, and their degrees retain actual nilpotent lengths. The two Stokes calculations have the stated signs and apply to arbitrary complementary forms: ∫aDe=−∫d'a∧d''e=∫Da∧e. No symmetric Green formula is required. Adding the fixed scalar a's moments preserves the restriction-zero condition, so the undifferentiated collar estimate controls eδ∧Da. Compact smooth approximation of h, combined with the independently obtained uniform variation bound, completes the continuous-multiplier step.

The finite separable reduction uses an actual finite normal closure, without requiring it to lie in M. Reverse canonical measure projection descends the result from that closure without a degree factor. The purely inseparable proof descends both units and inverses through Frobenius in the unreduced tensor algebra. The homeomorphism of carriers, the identity t_f=q^-1 t_g, and the q^{-(a+b)} exterior scaling establish every bidegree. The mixed tower is an embedded separable-then-purely-inseparable tower, and finite tensor associativity identifies its actual scalar spaces.

Sections 7–8 establish exact completion descent. Density is used in the actual completed tensor norm, and the finite associativity maps are bounded inverses on dense elementary tensors. Scalar surjectivity is reconstructed through valued embeddings into a completed algebraic closure of H(x); no injectivity of A⊗M is presumed. The positive weighted maximum in (15) gives a uniform perturbation threshold. When |g|≥δ, all valid weak, strict, and equality comparisons are preserved. When |g|<δ, an unchanged numerator keeps the whole system false. Consequently the actual rational domain and its strict locus descend exactly. The universal domain property identifies their analytic structures, including nilpotents.

Unit and inverse bounds can be made explicit within the approximation choice already allowed in Section 8: choose ||u_j−f_j|| smaller than both min|f_j| and ||f_j^{-1}||^{-1}. Neumann inversion then gives ||u_j^{-1}|| upstairs ≤||f_j^{-1}||. Independently, scalar surjectivity and the affinoid spectrum criterion make u_j an actual finite-stage unit, whose inverse belongs to the actual finite-stage Banach algebra. This is a quantitative clarification of the permitted approximation choice, not a replacement argument. Equality of logarithmic scalar sections implies equality of both derivatives by compact-image nullity and the sheaf calculus, so the higher-form conclusion is exact rather than a derivative-approximation claim.

The descended strict loci are ordinary opens of the entire finite-stage space because their enclosing domains lie inside the inverse image of a downstairs ordinary interior. After taking one common finite field, the finite compact partition and zero extensions yield one compact form whose pullback equals β globally, including β's zero regions. No saturation of the original support or agreement of local descendants on overlaps is assumed. Compact inverse images and the optional local pullback-faithfulness argument are both reconstructed correctly; no compact inverse-limit theorem is needed.

The completion-purity argument is valid. A hypothetical point of local dimension m<n has a rational neighborhood avoiding every component of dimension greater than m. That neighborhood descends exactly to a nonempty finite-stage domain. Finite-stage purity makes its analytic dimension n, including when its auxiliary radii are non-strict; complete scalar dimension invariance contradicts its upstairs dimension bound. This establishes local dimension n at every point. Spectral surjectivity then supplies a point with each minimal-prime kernel, lying on that component alone, and proves that every upstairs minimal component has dimension n. No simultaneous normalization, completed-module injection, or unproved Tate flatness is used.

Finally, the pairings in (21) apply scalar projection only to differentiated smooth top forms and then integrate a bounded continuous multiplier on their compact supports. The converse uses compact pullbacks of downstairs tests. The Artinian composition-series calculation in (22) preserves the sum of local lengths times residue-field degrees under arbitrary complete field extension. It supplies exactly the finite-fibre degree calculation used in canonical calibration projection. Same-carrier restriction and scalar projection therefore remain distinct, including in wild and inseparable cases.

There are harmless source wording and typography corrections that should be recorded. CLD 3.3.10 prints the wrong commutation exponent; the correct exponent is (p+q)(p'+q'), directly confirmed by the exterior-algebra definition in 1.1.1 and used correctly in Section 5. The rational localization formula in 11.1.5 must retain the ambient algebra A. The composition formulas in 11.4.1 require g^{-1}(Int(Y/X)). The Artinian branch of 13.3.3 needs dim_y(Y)=0. In 15.3.1's proof, the target volume form is the downstairs one. In 5.10.1(a), the displayed relation is equality, as its proof states. A.2.3 reverses the initial cutoff values and writes y where f(y) is required; A.2.4 should choose its compact neighborhood inside a point-separating open so the functions used at its boundary are defined. Section 3.4 independently gives the required affinoid cutoff proof with the correct values and domains. These corrections do not alter the transport argument or require a new proof of Theorems A or B.

No indispensable mathematical obligation remains unclosed in this partial scope. Compilation, finite diagnostics, catalogue comparisons, priority assertions, and artifact-integrity claims were not used as proof certification.

passages.statement: For a complete non-Archimedean field k, the spectrum of a k-affinoid Banach algebra A is compact Hausdorff; A is noetherian with closed ideals, and M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective. For x∈M(A), H(x) is the completion of Frac(A/ker(x)) with its induced absolute value. Consequently an element having no analytic zero is a unit in A, without a reducedness hypothesis. CLD 11.1.1–2.
passages.quote: Si A est une k-algèbre affinoïde l’application continue naturelle de M (A) vers Spec A est surjective ([9], Proposition 2.1.1).

passages.statement: For a k-affinoid algebra A, a system |f_i|≤r_i|g| with r_i>0 and no common analytic zero defines a rational affinoid domain, and g is invertible on that domain. Every point of M(A) has a rational neighborhood contained in any prescribed ordinary open neighborhood, with every defining inequality strict at that point. CLD 11.1.5.
passages.quote: Tout point de X possède une base de voisinages rationnels, en particulier une base de voisinages affinoïdes. Plus précisément, pour tout x ∈ X et tout voisinage ouvert U de x, il existe un système rationnel d’inéquations β dont le lieu de validité est contenu dans U , et tel que x satisfasse β̊.

passages.statement: Good k-analytic spaces have affinoid neighborhood bases. Ordinary opens are analytic domains, and every analytic domain has its canonical analytic structure and the universal factorization property for morphisms whose images lie in that domain. CLD 11.1.7.
passages.quote: Tout morphisme f : Y → X se factorisant ensemblistement par V se factorise en fait uniquement par la structure analytique de V .

passages.statement: Over a complete nontrivially valued field k, every point of a good strict k-analytic space has a strictly affinoid neighborhood. CLD 11.7.7.
passages.quote: Autrement dit tout point d’un bon espace strictement k-analytique admet un voisinage strictement affinoïde

passages.statement: For a k-affinoid algebra A, finite A-algebras admit their finite-module affinoid Banach topology, uniquely up to equivalence of norms; a finite A-module presentation supplies that topology. Finite analytic morphisms are boundaryless and are stable under analytic base change. CLD 11.4.4.
passages.quote: Le foncteur d’oubli de la norme induit une équivalence de catégories entre A-algèbres de Banach finies et A-algèbres finies

For an affinoid space with minimal components X_i, local dimension at x is max_{x∈X_i}dim(X_i). An analytic domain V⊂X satisfies dim_x(V)=dim_x(X) for every x∈V, and analytic dimension is the supremum of local dimensions. CLD 11.2.3.

For analytic morphisms Z→Y→X, relative interiors satisfy Int(Z/Y)∩g^{-1}(Int(Y/X))⊂Int(Z/X), with equality when Y→X is locally separated. The relative interior of an analytic-domain inclusion is its ordinary topological interior. Relative interiors satisfy the analytic base-change inclusion, including complete field extension; hence boundarylessness is preserved by such base change. CLD 11.4.1.

On a Hausdorff analytic space, every ordinary smooth form of any nonnegative bidegree has, on an ordinary open cover, descriptions as pullbacks of coefficient superforms by moments given by finite tuples of analytic units. Ordinary smooth forms form sheaves for the ordinary topology and are stable under wedge, J, d′ and d″. CLD 6.2.1–2 and 15.1.1(b).

For a finite-dimensional real affine space V, a paralinear subset P, and an ambient open U, smooth superforms on P∩U admit ambient smooth representatives modulo restriction-zero forms whenever P∩U is closed in U. Tropical coefficient descriptions admit such representatives after choosing a suitable ambient open. CLD 1.9.4 and 3.3.3.

Smooth superform sheaves carry the exterior-algebra product, total-degree Leibniz rules, d′²=d″²=0, d′d″=−d″d′, and the identities Jd′=d″J and Jd″=−d′J. Pullback by a G-tropical morphism respects wedge, J, and both differentials. CLD 1.1.1, 1.3.6, 1.9.8 and 3.3.10–12, with the commutation exponent in 3.3.10 interpreted according to 1.1.1.

For a G-tropical chart f:X→E and a coefficient form α on a paralinear subset containing f(X), f*α is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when α restricts to zero on f(V) for every compact analytic domain V⊂X. CLD Proposition 3.4.4.

Let k be complete non-Archimedean, Γ⊂R_{>0} a subgroup with |k*|Γ nontrivial, X a compact Γ-strict k-analytic space of dimension d, and f a finite tuple of analytic units. Then |f|(X) is a c-polytope of dimension at most d, where c=(Q,(|k*|Γ)^Q). No reducedness, smoothness, or perfectness hypothesis is required. Ducros, Theorem 3.2(1).

A moment on a compact Hausdorff analytic space of level n is pleasant. Its characteristic skeleton admits compatible cell refinements with its image, using convenient moment cells and a strong image-cell decomposition; in the compact case the relevant decomposition can be chosen finite. CLD 5.4.4 and 14.1.8, 14.1.11–12.

Let X be an analytic space of level n, f:X→T a moment, C a convenient n-dimensional f-cell, and q:T→G_m^n a torus morphism whose tropicalization is injective on f_trop(C). Then q∘f has relative dimension zero on C and is finite flat of one constant positive degree d_C on C's cell interior. The canonical calibration there is d_C(q∘f)_trop*e, with positive standard volume e; image-cell calibrations sum the corresponding sheet calibrations. These degrees are actual fibre-algebra degrees and require no reducedness or separability assumption. CLD 14.2.2, 14.3.2–5 and 14.5.1–2.

On a canonically calibrated G-tropical space of level n, top G-forms define skeletal volume densities compatibly with analytic domains. Tropical Borel top forms define Borel variation measures; locally integrable ones define signed Radon measures satisfying |ω_Rad|=ω_Bor. Smooth top forms are locally integrable and compact smooth top forms are integrable. Pleasant-chart integration is integration against the pushed-forward canonical calibration. CLD 5.8.1–5 and 5.10.1.

For a Hausdorff analytic space X of level n, a skeletal subset Σ and a complete extension l/k, skeletal scalar extension Σ_l→Σ is a surjective piecewise immersion preserving local dimension and compatible with moment characteristic skeleta. Its canonical calibration satisfies p_*μ_l=μ, without a field-degree factor. CLD 12.9.11 and 14.3.6.

For a finite valued extension F/k and an actual F-analytic space X of level n, viewing the same carrier as k-analytic preserves analytic dimension and skeletal subsets. Its canonical calibrations satisfy μ_k=[F:k]μ_F. CLD Remark 14.4.3.

For a Hausdorff analytic space X of level n, a complete extension l/k and scalar projection p:X_l→X, every tropical Borel top G-form ω satisfies p_*((p*ω)_Bor,l)=ω_Bor,k. If ω is locally integrable, p_*((p*ω)_Rad,l)=ω_Rad,k. Neither identity has a field-degree factor. CLD Proposition 15.3.1.

On a tropical space of level n, a locally integrable real multiplier u and a smooth G-form ω define an order-zero current by α↦∫u(ω∧α)_Rad against compact ordinary complementary smooth tests, compatibly with localization. In particular this construction applies to finite continuous multipliers. CLD 7.3.5.

Every Hausdorff pure n-dimensional analytic space, equipped with its canonical affine G-tropical structure, calibration and analytic boundary, is a tropical space of level n. This tropical structure agrees with the structure induced on each analytic domain. CLD Theorem 15.7.1 and 15.7.2.

On a calibrated G-tropical space of level n, every compact C1 G-form η of type (n−1,n) satisfies ∫d′η=∫∂η. The J identities supply the double-prime version. For ordinary forms on a boundaryless tropical space, the boundary integrals vanish. CLD Proposition 5.11.1(a), together with the ordinary tropical-space boundary structure.
